title: Three Years and One Short Plan
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：temple　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 temple 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the planner ① visited the temple that no citizen in the district would have measured, and he said the visiting was the whole of the year. The ② temple, meaning the shrine itself and not the plan, ran three years and stayed unmeasured in the book; a temple, he said, is the only thing in a district that is judged by how long it is left unmeasured.

Every ③ temple in that district had the same short plan beside it, and the ④ temple at the far square, meaning the plot they kept for the children to measure and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A temple, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to measure; the planner said the measuring is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the temple was the whole of the matter, meaning the faith and not the shrine. The ⑥ temple, meaning the faith and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody measures; temple, he said, is either something you visit or the only word that means both a shrine and a faith. He said the faith is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ temple had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short plan. The ⑧ temple of the whole thing, the planner wrote in March, was one district and three years of measuring; temple, he said, is either the plot at the far square or the reason you learned to measure. He said the measuring was never mentioned.

The ⑨ temple I remember is the shrine measured in the report, which closed in 1964 and is still measured as the quietest in the district. A ⑩ temple, my mother said in 1966, is the only shrine that improves by being measured; every temple, she said, is a faith that has agreed to look like a shrine. She said the faith was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 寺庙；庙宇（指街区里每一座旁边的那一座）
B. n. 寺庙；庙宇（指那座寺庙本身，与薄薄的图纸相对）
C. 固定搭配：visit the temple 进这一座寺庙
D. n. 寺庙；庙宇（指留给孩子们丈量的那一块）
E. n. 寺庙之事（抽象总称，指一处街区的寺庙之事）
F. n. 寺庙；庙宇（指规划报告里写到、被测量的那一座）
G. n. 寺庙、信仰（指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 信仰（抽象总称，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: visited the temple that no citizen in the district would have measured
The temple, meaning the shrine itself and not the plan
the temple at the far square
the temple was the whole of the matter
the temple had become a line in a report
The temple of the whole thing
A temple, my mother said in 1966

answers.why: visit the temple 意为“进这一座寺庙”，1957 年那位规划员把街区里没有一位市民肯测量的一座寺庙做了一遍。
temple 意为“寺庙；庙宇”，指那座寺庙本身而不是薄薄的图纸，它经过了三个年份而在簿子上没有被测量。
temple 意为“寺庙；庙宇”，指街区里每一座旁边的那一座，每一座旁边都有同一张薄薄的图纸。
temple 意为“寺庙；庙宇”，指最远那处广场的留给孩子们丈量的那一块，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
temple 意为“寺庙、信仰”，指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这座信仰就是那件事的全部。
temple 意为“信仰”，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西而不是那座寺庙，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
temple 意为“寺庙；庙宇”，指规划报告里写到、被测量的那一座，到 1962 年这一座成了规划报告里的一行。
temple 意为“寺庙之事”，规划员三月写道，整件事的寺庙之事是一处街区和三个年份的测量。
temple 意为“寺庙；庙宇”，我记得的是规划报告里测量过的那一座，1964 年落成了，至今仍被说成街区里最安静的一座。
temple 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，寺庙是唯一会因为被好好测量而变得更好的寺庙。
